text: First, the Weighted Fusion mechanism combines feature representations extracted from multiple levels.
Four distinct level features from the image encoder serve as the inputs.
Each feature is scaled by a preset weighting factor.
These weighted feature vectors are then summed together.
The accumulated sum is normalized by dividing by the total sum of the weights.
This produces the final fused multi-level feature representation.
Alternatively, the Learnable Fusion mechanism fuses features in a data-driven manner.
The four multi-level feature vectors are again taken as inputs.
Here, all input features are concatenated across the channel dimension into a single joint representation.
A learnable adapter processes and reduces the dimensionality of the concatenated features.
This yields the final enhanced fused feature vector.
